title: Health is public, and says the same thing to everyone

expect.why: Health is the liveness probe. A load balancer has no token, so a server that refuses an anonymous probe is a server nothing can route to.
The field the probe reads. Every port answers the same word or the probe means something different per deployment.
How a probe tells this service from whatever else is on the port.
A boolean, not the number one and not the string true — a client keying on it must not have to guess.
Readiness is separate from liveness and both are reported here.
Its value is volatile, but a port that omits it entirely has dropped a field an operator's dashboard reads.
Which store is behind the control plane is part of what health reports; the value differs by deployment, the field does not.
Presenting a token must not change a public endpoint's answer.
The client library's own reading of a 200, which is the thing a consumer branches on.
The same answer through the client library as over raw HTTP.
A public endpoint does not validate what it does not require. A server that 401s an unparseable token here would fail probes during any key rotation.
